result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B keeps the concept and deals with the real problems: it removes the gradient and shadow, thickens the strokes, and replaces Papyrus while flagging that swap as a decision for the user. It also says why the mark holds up in one color and at small sizes. A keeps the shadow, the gradient and Papyrus, so the main usability problems are still there. B's one weakness is that it promises one-color and favicon versions instead of supplying them. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A keeps the concept and fixes the problems that would show up in real use. It drops the gradient and shadow, thickens the hairlines, replaces Papyrus with a reliable bold sans and gives a reason for each change, though it only describes the one-color and small-size versions instead of showing them. B keeps the gradient, the drop shadow and Papyrus, so the main issues stay unfixed, and it says nothing about using the logo in a single color.
